- (2) $F_{X*}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ , considered as a sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , is an Azumaya algebra of rank1111 11 A priori this is a locally constant function on $X$ . $p^{2\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ .

#### Proof.

Both statements are local (e.g. in Zariski topology) and so we can assume $X\simeq(F_{Y}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})^{-1}(Z)$ where $Y$ is smooth over $S$ and $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed subscheme. In this case, $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ is a central reduction of $\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ via an embedding $T^{*}Y^{(1)}|_{Z}\hookrightarrow T^{*}Y^{(1)}\simeq(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . More precisely, let $i\colon X\hookrightarrow Y$ be the embedding. Following the proof of Lemma 2.32 in this situation we have isomorphisms $\Omega^{1}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\Omega^{1}_{Y}$ , and consequently, $\mathcal{T}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\mathcal{T}_{Y}$ . By naturality, the latter is an isomorphism of Lie algebroids, and induces an isomorphism $\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq i^{*}\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ . Also

$$ \Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{O}_{Z} $$

and so $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ can be identified with the restriction of $(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ to $Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Moreover, if we denote by $i_{Z}\colon Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ the corresponding embedding, applying $F_{X*}$ we get

$$ F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}(i^{*}\mathcal{D}_{Y})\simeq i_{Z}^{*}F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}\simeq F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{O}_{Z}\simeq F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}\otimes_{\mathcal{O}_{(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\mathcal{O}_{(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}, $$

where in the last isomorphism we considered $F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{Y}$ as an Azumaya algebra over $(T^{*}Y)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Thus we get that $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ as a sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a restriction of an Azumaya algebra, and as such is an Azumaya algebra itself. Its center then also is necessarily isomorphic to $\mathcal{O}_{(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\simeq\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . ∎

#### Remark 2.39.

From the proof of Proposition 2.35 it also follows that $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon X\rightarrow X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a finite faithfully flat map of degree $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ . Indeed, it is locally obtained as a base change of relative Frobenius for a smooth scheme $Y$ of (relative) dimension $\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}$ (see Remark 2.33).

### 2.6. De Rham complex and Cartier operation

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth scheme over $S$ . Put $r\coloneqq\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}$ ; this is a locally constant function on $X$ . Consider the de Rham complex

$$ \mathrm{dR}_{X}\coloneqq\left[0\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X}\rightarrow\ldots\rightarrow\Omega^{r}_{X}\rightarrow 0\right]{:} $$

this is a complex of sheaves of $\mathcal{O}_{S}$ -modules on $X$ with differential given by the (relative) de Rham differential. Since the relative de Rham differential is $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{p}\cdot B$ -linear, the pushforward $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X}$ defines a complex of coherent sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

Let $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{*}\coloneqq\mathcal{H}^{*}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X})$ denote the sheaf cohomology algebra of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X}$ . Recall the notation $\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\coloneqq W_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\Omega^{1}_{X}$ . One can define the inverse Cartier morphism

$$ C^{-1}\colon\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\!(\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X})\rightarrow\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{*} $$

as follows. Namely in degree 0 it is given by $(F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}\colon\mathcal{O}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\rightarrow F_{X*}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , while in degree 1 locally one sends $(W_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}})^{-1}(df)\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ to $[f^{p-1}df]\in\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{1}$ . By a standard computation the latter gives a well-defined additive map to $\mathcal{H}^{1}_{\mathrm{dR},X}$ , which is $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ -linear. For higher degrees $C^{-1}$ uniquely extends by multiplicativity.

The classical result of Cartier states that $C^{-1}$ is an equivalence if $X$ over $S$ is smooth. This remains true in the pseudo-smooth setting as well.

#### Proposition 2.40.

Let $X$ be a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme. Then the inverse Cartier map is an isomorphism.

#### Proof.

We deduce the statement from the smooth case. The statement is Zariski local, so we can assume $X=(F_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(Z)$ is as in Lemma 2.32 (so $Y$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow Y^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ ). In this case $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq Z$ . Let $i\colon X\hookrightarrow Y$ and $i^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\colon Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . By Remarks 2.33, 2.34 and base change, $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{X}$ can be naturally identified with $i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{Y}$ . By Cartier isomorphism in the smooth case, the cohomology sheaves $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},Y}^{*}$ are isomorphic to $\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{Y}$ ; in particular, they are vector bundles and thus are flat over $\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . From this and Remark 2.34 we get that

$$ \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},X}^{*}\simeq\mathcal{H}^{*}(i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}F_{Y*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathrm{dR}_{Y})\simeq i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{dR},Y}^{*}\simeq i^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}*}(\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{Y}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\!\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{Y})\simeq\wedge^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}.\qed $$

Let $C$ be the inverse to $C^{-1}$ . In each degree $i$ , $C$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal{H}^{i}_{\mathrm{dR},X}\simeq\Omega^{i,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ which we can precompose with the projection $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{i}_{X,cl}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{H}^{i}_{\mathrm{dR},X}$ from the closed $i$ -forms. We will call the resulting map $\mathsf{C}^{i}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{i}_{X,cl}\twoheadrightarrow\Omega^{i,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ the Cartier operation. For $i=1$ one gets a short exact sequence

$$ 0\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}/\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\xrightarrow{d}F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\xrightarrow{\mathsf{C}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow 0, $$

of sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ where the term on the left is identified with the exact 1-forms via $d$ .

#### Remark 2.41.

The map $\mathsf{C}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ dually induces a map $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\otimes F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ which lifts the pairing map $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\otimes\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Substituting a local section $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ we obtain the corresponding “contraction” maps

$$ \widetilde{\iota_{\xi}}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\ \ \text{ and }\ \ \iota_{\xi}\colon\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}. $$

Following [BK], we have the following explicit formula for $\widetilde{\iota_{\xi}}$ . Namely, given a closed 1-form $\omega\in\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ and a vector field $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ (giving a section $\xi^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\coloneqq(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\xi)\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ ) one has the following formula

$$ \widetilde{\iota_{\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}(\mathsf{C}(\omega))=\langle\xi^{[p]},\omega\rangle-\xi^{p-1}(\langle\xi,\omega\rangle) $$

for the corresponding contraction.

### 2.7. Line bundles with connection and Milne’s exact sequence

Let $(\mathcal{E},\nabla)$ , with $\nabla\colon\mathcal{E}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}\otimes\Omega^{1}_{X}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf with flat connection on a pseudo-smooth $S$ -scheme $X$ . The connection $\nabla$ induces a map $\mathcal{D}_{X}\rightarrow\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{E})$ , whose restriction to $Z(\mathcal{D}_{X})$ factors through the subalgebra of $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -linear endomorphisms $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})^{\nabla^{\prime}=0}\subset\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{E})$ that are flat with respect to the natural connection1212 12 Here the connection $\nabla^{\prime}$ on $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ is given by $(\nabla^{\prime}(\psi))(s)\coloneqq\nabla(\psi(s))-\psi(\nabla(s)$ for $s\in\mathcal{E}$ and $\psi\in\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ . Thus an endomorphism $\psi\in\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ is flat with respect to $\nabla^{\prime}$ if and only if it commutes with the action of $\mathcal{T}_{X}$ induced by $\nabla$ . on $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{E})$ . Indeed, central elements commute both with multiplication on functions and action by vector fields.

#### Construction 2.42 ( $p$ -curvature map for line bundles).

Let $\mathcal{E}\coloneqq\mathcal{L}$ in $(\mathcal{E},\nabla)$ be a line bundle. In this case, the endomorphism sheaf $(\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{L}),\nabla^{\prime})$ with its natural connection is given by $(\mathcal{O}_{X},d)$ . In particular, $\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}}(\mathcal{L})^{\nabla^{\prime}=0}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ is given by $\ker d$ , which is identified with $\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\subset\mathcal{O}_{X}$ by Proposition 2.40. Using the $p$ -curvature map (2.2) we obtain a map of sheaves $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rightarrow\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , or, in other words, a section of $\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ , which we will denote $\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L},\nabla)\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}$ . It is not hard to see from the definition (and the way $\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\subset Z(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ acts on the tensor product), that

$$ \mathsf{c}_{p}((\mathcal{L}_{1},\nabla_{1})\otimes(\mathcal{L}_{2},\nabla_{2}))=\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L}_{1},\nabla_{1})+\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L}_{2},\nabla_{2}). $$

If we are given a trivialization $\mathcal{L}\simeq\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , $\nabla$ can be written in the form $d+\alpha$ for some closed 1-form $\alpha\in\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ . Restricting to line bundles of this form we get a map of sheaves

$$ \mathsf{c}_{p}\colon F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\rightarrow\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X},\ \ \ \ \mathsf{c}_{p}\colon\alpha\mapsto\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha). $$

Since $(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha_{1})\otimes(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha_{2})\simeq(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha_{1}+\alpha_{2})$ the above map is a map of sheaves of abelian groups.

#### Remark 2.43.

One has an explicit formula for the map $\mathsf{c}_{p}$ in terms of the Cartier operation. Namely, given $\alpha\in\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ let’s compute the pairing $\langle\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha)\rangle$ for any $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}$ , $\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\in(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\xi)\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ : this will define $\mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha)$ uniquely. By definition, we need to compute the action of $\theta(\xi)=\xi^{p}-\xi^{[p]}$ on line bundle $(\mathcal{O}_{X},d+\alpha)$ . This is given by

$$ (\xi+\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle)^{p}-\xi^{[p]}-\langle\xi^{[p]},\alpha\rangle=\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle^{p}-\langle\xi^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\mathsf{C}(\alpha)\rangle\in\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{S}}(\mathcal{O}_{X}) $$

where for the equality we used that $\xi^{p}-\xi^{[p]}$ acts by 0 on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ , formula (2.4) and also Jacobson’s formula. Note that $\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle^{p}=(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle)=\langle\xi^{{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}},\alpha^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\rangle$ , where $\alpha^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\coloneqq(W_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}\alpha$ . This gives

$$ \mathsf{c}_{p}(\alpha)=\alpha^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}-\mathsf{C}(\alpha). $$

We now consider a non-commutative counterpart of the above $p$ -curvature map.

#### Construction 2.44 (Central reductions of $\mathcal{D}_{X}$ associated to 1-forms).

Let $\alpha\in H^{0}(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}},\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X})$ be a global section. Let $i_{\alpha}\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ be the graph of $\alpha$ . Under the identification $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\simeq\Spec_{X}\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , the image $\Gamma_{\alpha}=\im(i_{\alpha})\subset(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ of $i_{\alpha}$ is defined by the sheaf of ideals generated by linear expressions

$$ \mathcal{I}_{\alpha}\coloneqq(\xi-\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle)_{\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\subset\Sym^{*}_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}. $$

We denote by $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}\coloneqq i_{\alpha}^{*}(F_{X*}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ the corresponding pull-back of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ considered as a sheaf of algebras over $(T^{*}\!X)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . For any $\alpha$ the sheaf $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ defines an Azumaya algebra over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ of rank $p^{2\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ .

#### Construction 2.45 (Line bundles with connection vs splittings.).

Suppose we are given a line bundle with flat connection $(\mathcal{L},\nabla)$ and put $\alpha\coloneqq\mathsf{c}_{p}(\mathcal{L},\nabla)$ . Then by definition of $\mathsf{c}_{p}$ we have that $\xi\in\mathcal{T}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ acts on $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}$ by $\langle\xi,\alpha\rangle\in\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . It follows that the action of $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}$ on $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}$ induced by $\nabla$ factors through $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ . Moreover, by Remark 2.39 $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}$ is a vector bundle of rank $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ and thus is a splitting bundle for $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ : namely, $\nabla$ induces an isomorphism

$$ \nabla\colon\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}). $$

Vice versa, let $\mathcal{E}$ be a splitting bundle $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ -module on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Then $\mathcal{E}$ is a vector bundle of rank $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ . However $\mathcal{E}$ is also a quasi-coherent $F_{X*}\mathcal{O}_{X}$ -module (with the action via the composition $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha})$ and so comes as a pushforward $(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})\mathcal{F}$ of some quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ . Since $F_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is a finite locally free map of degree $p^{\rk\Omega^{1}_{X}}$ the only option is that $\mathcal{F}\simeq(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(\mathcal{E})$ is a line bundle. The action of $\mathcal{D}_{X}\simeq(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{-1}(F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{D}_{X})$ on $\mathcal{F}$ induces a natural flat connection, whose $p$ -curvature is given by $\alpha$ . Moreover, isomorphisms between two line bundles $(\mathcal{L}_{1},\nabla_{1})$ and $(\mathcal{L}_{2},\nabla_{2})$ with the same $p$ -curvature $\alpha$ exactly correspond to isomorphisms between the corresponding $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ -modules $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}_{1}$ and $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{L}_{2}$ . In particular, any two such line bundles a étale (and, in fact even Zariski) locally isomorphic.

This gives an equivalence of two groupoids: line bundles with flat connection on $X$ with $p$ -curvature $\alpha$ , and splitting bundles1313 13 Here an object is given by a vector bundle $\mathcal{E}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ together with an isomorphism $\gamma\colon\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}\simeq\mathcal{E}nd_{\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\mathcal{E})$ , and morphisms are isomorphisms of vector bundles that preserve this data. for $\mathcal{D}_{X,\alpha}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ correspondingly.

Consider the map $d\log\colon\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}\rightarrow\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ of étale sheaves on $\mathcal{O}_{X}$ sending $f$ to $df/f$ . It induces a map of étale sheaves $F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}$ on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ .

There is a short exact sequence of étale sheaves on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$

$$ 0\rightarrow F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times}/(\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})^{\times}\xrightarrow{d\log}F_{X*}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\Omega^{1}_{X,cl}\xrightarrow{\mathsf{c}_{p}}\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{X}\rightarrow 0, $$
