#### Construction 3.25 (Restricted structure on the Frobenius neighborhood).

We endow $X=\Spec A_{0}(R)$ with the structure of a restricted symplectic $R$ -scheme as in Construction 2.63. Namely, we consider $(X,[\eta_{\mathsf{can}}])$ with

$$ \eta_{\mathsf{can}}\coloneqq\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_{i}dx_{i}\in\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}. $$

The corresponding symplectic from is given by $\omega\coloneqq d\eta_{\mathsf{can}}=\sum_{i}dy_{i}\wedge dx_{i}\in\Omega^{2}_{A_{0}(R)}$ .

For the lemma that will follow shortly we will need the following generalization of Definition 2.58.

#### Definition 3.26.

Let $X$ be a symplectic $S$ -scheme. A derivation $\xi\in H^{0}(X,\mathcal{T}_{X})$ is called $\log$ -Hamiltonian if $\xi=f^{-1}\cdot H_{f}$ for some $f\in H^{0}(X,\mathcal{O}_{X}^{\times})$ .

#### Remark 3.27.

Similarly to the Hamiltonian case, the condition $\xi=f^{-1}\cdot H_{f}$ is equivalent to $\iota_{\xi}\omega=d\log f$ .

Given a vector field $\xi\in H^{0}(X,\mathcal{T}_{X})$ we denote by $L_{\xi}\colon\Omega^{i}_{X}\rightarrow\Omega^{i}_{X}$ the Lie derivative along $\xi$ . We recall the Cartan formula: $L_{\xi}=\iota_{\xi}\circ d+d\circ\iota_{\xi}$ in terms of the de Rham differential and contraction. A vector field $\xi$ is called Poisson if $L_{\xi}\omega=0$ .

#### Lemma 3.28.

- (1) A Poisson vector field $\xi\in{\mathcal{T}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ is Hamiltonian if and only if for all $f\in A_{0}(R)$ we have

$$ \xi(f^{[p]})=H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f)). $$

- (2) A Poisson derivation $\xi\in{\mathcal{T}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ is $\log$ -Hamiltonian if and only if for all $f\in A$ we have (3.5)

$$ \xi(f^{[p]})=H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f))\ +\ \xi(f)^{p}. $$

#### Proof.

The proof essentially follows [BK, Lemma 2.5]. By Cartan formula and the assumption $L_{\xi}\omega=0\Rightarrow d(\iota_{\xi}\omega)+0=0$ we get that $\beta\coloneqq\iota_{\xi}\omega\in\Omega^{1}_{A_{0}(R)}$ is closed. By Remark 2.59 and Lemma 3.21 $\xi$ is Hamiltonian if and only if $\mathsf{C}(\beta)=0$ . Similarly, by Lemma 3.23 $\xi$ is $\log$ -Hamiltonian if and only if $\mathsf{C}(\beta)=\beta^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ . Since $\omega$ is non-degenerate, Hamiltonian vector fields generate $\mathcal{T}_{A_{0}(R)}$ . Then vector fields of the form $H_{f}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ generate $\mathcal{T}_{A_{0}(R)}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , and so it is enough to understand the pairing of $\mathsf{C}(\beta)\in\Omega^{1,{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}_{A_{0}(R)}$ with (the twists of) Hamiltonian vector fields. By Remark 2.41 $\iota_{H_{f}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\mathsf{C}(\beta))=\langle H_{f}^{[p]},\beta\rangle-H_{f}^{p-1}(\langle{H_{f}},\beta\rangle)$ . Substituting $\beta=\iota_{\xi}\omega$ we get $\iota_{H_{f}}(\mathsf{C}(\beta))=\xi(f^{[p]})-H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f))\in R\subset A_{0}(R)$ . Thus, $\mathsf{C}(\beta)=0$ if and only if $\xi(f^{[p]})-H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi(f))=0$ for all $f\in A_{0}(R)$ . This gives Part 1. Part 2 is obtained similarly, by noting that $\iota_{H_{f}^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}(\beta^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}})=(\iota_{H_{f}}\beta)^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}=\xi(f)^{p}$ . ∎

### 3.5. $h$ -separable algebras

Let $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ be the category of schemes over $\mathbb{S}$ . To construct a group action on the category of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ -modules it will be crucial to have some understanding of the algebra automorphisms of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . This will become easier if we restrict to a certain subcategory in $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ , where automorphisms of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ are closely related to $G_{0}$ . The goal of this section is to define this subcategory.

#### Construction 3.29.

Let $R\in\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}$ . For an element $b\in R/h$ let $\tilde{b}\in R$ be a lift. Then the operation $b\mapsto\tilde{b}^{p}$ gives a well-defined map $R/h\rightarrow R/h^{p}$ . Indeed, given other lift $\tilde{b}^{\prime}=\tilde{b}+hc$ we have $(\tilde{b}^{\prime})^{p}=\tilde{b}^{p}+h^{p}c^{p}$ .

Consider $\alpha_{p}(R/h)=\{a\in R/h\ |\ a^{p}=0\}\subset R/h$ . Then restricting the above map to $\alpha_{p}(R/h)$ gives a map $\delta\colon\alpha_{p}(R/h)\rightarrow hR/h^{p}R$ .

#### Definition 3.30.

An $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebra $R$ is called $h$ -separable if

- (1) it is $h$ -torsion free (equivalently, flat over $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ );

- (2) the map $\delta_{R}\colon\alpha_{p}(R/h)\rightarrow hR/h^{p}R$ is equal to 0.

#### Remark 3.31.

It is not hard to see that the latter condition is equivalent to the following: for any $a\in R$ one has

$$ a^{p}\in hR\quad\Leftrightarrow\quad a^{p}\in h^{p}R. $$

We denote by $\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}^{h-\mathrm{sep}}$ the category of $h$ -separable $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebras.

#### Example 3.32.

- (1) Let $C$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -algebra. Then $R\coloneqq C\otimes_{\mathbb{F}_{p}}\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ is $h$ -separable. Indeed, it is $h$ -torsion free and to check the second condition note that $R/h\simeq C$ and any $x\in\alpha_{p}(R/h)$ can be lifted to $x\otimes 1$ for which $(x\otimes 1)^{p}=x^{p}\otimes 1=0$ . Thus $\delta_{R}$ is 0.

- (2) Any $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h,h^{-1}]$ -algebra $R$ is $h$ -separable. Indeed, it is obviously $h$ -tosion free and the second condition is vacuous since $R/h=0$ .

- (3) $R\coloneqq\mathbb{F}_{p}[h^{1/p}]$ is not $h$ separable. Indeed, $R/h\simeq\mathbb{F}_{p}[x]/x^{p}$ where $x$ is the class of $h^{1/p}$ , and the map $\delta_{R}$ sends $x$ to $h\in hR/h^{p}R$ .

Note that $\alpha_{p}(R/h)$ has a natural structure of $R$ -module such that $\delta_{R}$ is a Frobenius-linear map of $R$ -modules. Let $\delta_{R}^{\ell}\colon\alpha_{p}(R/h)\otimes_{R,F_{R}}R\rightarrow hR/h^{p}R$ be its linearization. Obviously, $\delta_{R}=0\Leftrightarrow\delta_{R}^{\ell}=0$ .

Even though it might not yet be clear what is the motivation behind the notion $h$ -separability, let us show that it is local in étale topology:

#### Lemma 3.33.

Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]$ -algebra and let $R\rightarrow R^{\prime}$ be an étale cover. Then $R$ is $h$ -separable if and only if $R^{\prime}$ is.

#### Proof.

$R^{\prime}$ is faithfully flat over $R$ , and so $R$ is $h$ -torsion free if and only if so is $R^{\prime}$ . It remains to relate $\delta_{R}$ and $\delta_{R^{\prime}}$ . Since $R\rightarrow R^{\prime}$ is étale, the relative Frobenius $F_{R^{\prime}/R}$ is an isomorphism. We have a factorization

$$ \textstyle{R\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{\id_{R}} \textstyle{R\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{R}} \textstyle{R\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \textstyle{R^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{F_{R^{\prime}}} \scriptstyle{F_{R^{\prime}/R}} \textstyle{R^{\prime}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces} \scriptstyle{W_{R^{\prime}/R}} \textstyle{R^{\prime}} $$

of $F_{R^{\prime}}$ as the composition $W_{R^{\prime}/R}\circ F_{R^{\prime}/R}$ (recall that $W_{R^{\prime}/R}$ by definition is the pull-back of $F_{R}$ to $R^{\prime}$ ). Identifying $\alpha_{p}(B)$ with the kernel of $F_{B}$ and the diagram above, it is not hard to see that the linearized map $\delta_{R^{\prime}}^{\ell}\colon\alpha_{p}(R^{\prime}/h)\otimes_{R^{\prime},F_{R^{\prime}}}R^{\prime}\rightarrow hR^{\prime}/h^{p}R^{\prime}$ is identified with $F_{R^{\prime}/R}^{-1}$ applied to the base change

$$ \delta_{R}^{\ell}\otimes R^{\prime}\colon\alpha_{p}(R/h)\otimes_{R,F_{R}}R\otimes_{R}R^{\prime}\rightarrow hR/h^{p}R\otimes_{R}R^{\prime}. $$

Thus, $\delta_{R^{\prime}}^{\ell}=0\Leftrightarrow\delta_{R}=0$ . ∎

#### Remark 3.34.

Let $R$ be an $h$ -separable $k[h]$ -algebra. Then for any $a\in R/h$ the image $\tilde{a}^{p}\in R/h^{p}$ only depends on the $p$ -th power $a^{p}\in R/h$ . We let ${\underline{\Aut}}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})$ be the sheaf on big fpqc site of $\mathbb{S}$ which sends $f\colon X\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ to algebra automorphisms of $f^{*}\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . #### Remark 3.38 (Poisson structure).

Let $R$ be $h$ -torsion free. Then $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is $h$ -torsion free as well and we can identify $h^{i}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{i+1}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\simeq A_{0}(R/h)$ (via dividing by $h^{i}$ ) for any $i\geq 0$ . The restricted $p$ -th power operation $-^{[p]}$ (corresponding to the restricted Poisson structure on $A_{0}(R)$ ) is more subtle to identify and this is where $h$ -separability property is important.

Note that for any $f\in A_{0}(R/h)$ and any lift $\tilde{f}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ the expression $\tilde{f}^{p}$ is well-defined mod $h^{p}$ . Indeed, by the Jacobson’s formula (see Section 2.2) we have

#### Lemma 3.42.

The map $\Ad\colon{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}\rightarrow{}\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ is a surjuction of Zariski sheaves on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!\!/\mathbb{S}}$ . The kernel of $\Ad(-)$ is canonically identified with ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

#### Proof.

Again, it is enough to prove the statement for the restrictions to $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ and $(\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}^{h-\mathrm{sep}})^{\mathrm{op}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ .

For $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ we have $\Ker(\mathsf{r})\simeq\underline{\Aut}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}})$ and we want to show that there is a short exact sequence

$$ 0\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{m}\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}^{\times}\rightarrow\Aut(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}})\rightarrow 0. $$

However, by Remark 3.16 we can identify $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ with the matrix algebra $\Mat_{p^{n}}$ , and the sequence above turns into

$$ 0\rightarrow\mathbb{G}_{m}\rightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p^{n}}\rightarrow\mathrm{PGL}_{p^{n}}\rightarrow 0, $$

which is exact in Zariski topology.

The case of $(\CAlg_{\mathbb{F}_{p}[h]/}^{h-\mathrm{sep}})^{\mathrm{op}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ is much more subtle. Let us first identify the kernel of $\Ad$ . By definition it consists of the invertible elements $Z({A}_{\mathbb{S}})^{\times}$ in the center. Every element $a\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ can be uniquely written as $\sum_{I,J}r_{I,J}x^{I}y^{J}$ with $r_{I,J}\in R$ (with $I=(i_{1},\ldots,i_{n})$ , $J=(j_{1},\ldots,j_{n})$ and $0\leq i_{k},j_{l}\leq p-1$ ). Since $R$ is $h$ -torsion free, from the relations defining $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ it is clear that is $r_{I,J}\neq 0$ for some non-zero $I$ or $J$ then there is $x_{i}$ , or $y_{j}$ such that one of the commutators $[a,x_{i}]$ or $[a,y_{j}]$ is non-zero. Thus $Z(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R))^{\times}\simeq R^{\times}$ and $\Ker(\Ad(-))\simeq{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

We now pass to showing that automorphisms of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ that are trivial modulo $h$ are given by conjugation, at least after a Zariski localization $R\rightarrow R^{\prime}$ . We will first prove this after inverting $h$ , then for $h$ -completion of $R$ and then will obtain the result for $R$ using Beauville-Laszlo gluing.

If $h\in R$ is invertible then $\Spec R$ lies over $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}$ , and we are done by the case $\Sch_{\!/\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}}\subset\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ .

If $R$ is $h$ -complete, note that $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ if also $h$ -complete (since it is free nodule of finite rank over $R$ ). We will approximate $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ by $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{n}$ for all $n\geq 0$ . As a base of induction let us show that any $\phi\in\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ is equal to an inner automorphism modulo $h^{2}$ . In other words, we would like to find $x\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)^{\times}$ such that $\phi=\Ad(x)\mod h^{2}$ . Note that the map $\phi-\id\mod h^{2}\colon A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}/h^{2}$ factors through $h\cdot A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ and gives a well defined map $\xi_{\phi}\colon A_{0}(R/h)\simeq A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}/h\rightarrow hA_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}/h^{2}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}\simeq A_{0}(R/h)$ , which is an $R/h$ -linear differentiation2222 22 Indeed,

$$ h\cdot\xi_{\phi}(xy)=\phi(\widetilde{x}\cdot\widetilde{y})-\widetilde{x}\cdot\widetilde{y}=\phi(\widetilde{x})\cdot\phi(\widetilde{y})-\widetilde{x}\cdot\widetilde{y}=h\cdot(\xi_{\phi}(x)\cdot y+x\cdot\xi_{\phi}(y))\pmod{h^{2}}. $$

of $A_{0}(R/h)$ . For $\phi=\Ad(x)$ with $x=x_{0}\mod h$ we have

$$ h\cdot\xi_{\Ad(x)}(a)=xax^{-1}-a=[x,a]\cdot x^{-1}=h\cdot\tfrac{1}{x_{0}}\{x_{0},a\}\pmod{h^{2}}, $$

and so one sees that $\xi_{\Ad(x)}=\frac{1}{x_{0}}H_{x_{0}}$ . Thus it is enough to show that for $\phi\in\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ the corresponding vector field $\xi_{\phi}$ is log-Hamiltonian.

The idea then is to use Lemma 3.28(2), namely we need to show that $\xi_{\phi}$ satisfies the corresponding equation (3.5). Looking at the action on commutator modulo $h^{2}$ , one sees that $\xi_{\phi}$ is Poisson (namely, $L_{\xi_{\phi}}\omega=0$ ), so Lemma 3.28(2) indeed can be applied. Moreover, it is enough to check (3.5) on $f\in I_{0}(R/h)=\{f\in A_{0}(R/h)\ |\ \ev_{0}(f)=0\}$ : indeed, the constants $R/h$ and $I_{0}(R/h)$ span all $A_{0}(R/h)$ . By 3.39, for $f\in I_{0}(R/h)$ and any lift $\tilde{f}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ we have

$$ \tilde{f}^{p}=h^{p-1}\cdot f^{[p]}\pmod{h^{p}}. $$

We then have

$$ h^{p}\cdot\xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=h^{p-1}\cdot(\phi(f^{[p]}-f^{[p]})=(\tilde{f}+h\cdot\widetilde{\xi_{\phi}(f)})^{p}-\tilde{f}^{p}\pmod{h^{p+1}}. $$

Using Jacobson’s formula (2.13) the right hand side is identified with $h^{p}(\xi_{\phi}(f)^{p}+L_{1}(\tilde{f},\widetilde{\xi_{\phi}(f)}))\pmod{h^{p+1}}$ . From this, using that $L_{1}(x,y)=\ad(x)^{p-1}(y)$ (2.14) and identifying $A_{0}(R/h)\simeq h^{p}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{p+1}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ , we get that

$$ \xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=\xi_{\phi}(f)^{p}+H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi_{\phi}(f)), $$

as desired.

For $n\geq 2$ one shows analogously that if $\phi\colon A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is an automorphism which is identity modulo $h^{n}$ then there exists an element $x\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ such that $\phi=\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)$ modulo $h^{n+1}$ . Namely, such $\phi$ also defines a derivation $\xi^{\prime}_{\phi}$ of $A_{0}(R/h)$ by considering the map $\phi-\id\mod h^{n+1}\colon A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\rightarrow A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{n+1}$ which factors through $A_{h}/h\simeq A_{0}$ and whose image lies in $h^{n}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)/h^{n+1}A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)\simeq A_{0}$ . As in the case of $n=1$ , looking at the action on the commutator one sees that $\xi^{\prime}_{\phi}$ is Poisson. However, we now have

$$ h^{n}\cdot\xi_{\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)}(a)=(1+h^{n-1}x)a(1-h^{n-1}x)=h^{n}\cdot[x_{0},a]\pmod{h^{n+1}}; $$

in other words, $\xi_{\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)}=H_{x_{0}}$ . Also, given $\phi$ that is trivial modulo $h^{n}$ with $n\geq 2$

$$ h^{p+n-1}\cdot\xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=h^{p-1}\cdot(\phi(f^{[p]}-f^{[p]})=(\tilde{f}+h^{n}\cdot\widetilde{\xi_{\phi}(f)})^{p}-\tilde{f}^{p}\pmod{h^{p+n}}, $$

from which (using Jacobson’s formula again) we get

$$ \xi_{\phi}(f^{[p]})=H_{f}^{p-1}(\xi_{\phi}(f)), $$

so by Lemma 3.28(1) $\xi_{\phi}$ is Hamiltonian and $\phi$ agrees with $\Ad(1+h^{n-1}x)$ for some $x$ .

This way, starting with an automorphism $\phi\in\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ , we can by induction construct a sequence of elements $x_{1},x_{2},x_{3},\ldots\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ such that

$$ \phi=\ldots\circ\Ad(1+h^{2}x_{3})\circ\Ad(1+hx_{2})\circ\Ad(x_{1})=\Ad(\ldots\cdot(1+h^{2}x_{3})(1+hx_{2})x_{1}), $$

where the infinite product on the right hand side is well-defined since $R$ is $h$ -complete.

Let now $R$ be an arbitrary $h$ -separable $k[h]$ -algebra. We are trying to show that the map of (Zariski) sheaves ${\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}}\rightarrow\Ker(\mathsf{r})$ on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ is surjective. It is enough to do so on stalks, and so we can assume $R$ is local (and, in particular, that $\Pic(R)=0$ ). Since $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is a free $R$ -module of finite rank, by Beauville-Laszlo theorem [BL], an $R$ -linear automorphism of $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R)$ is uniquely encoded by a pair of automorphisms $\phi_{1}\in\Aut_{R^{\wedge}_{h}}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}))$ , $\phi_{2}\in\Aut_{R[h^{-1}]}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}]))$ (where $R^{\wedge}_{h}$ is the $h$ -adic completion of $R$ ) such that their images in $\Aut_{R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]))$ agree. By the discussion above we can find elements $a_{1}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h})$ , $a_{2}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}])$ such that $\phi_{1}=\Ad(a_{1})$ and $\phi_{2}=\Ad(a_{2})$ ; moreover, if we denote by $a_{1}^{\circ}$ , $a_{2}^{\circ}$ the images of $a_{1}$ and $a_{2}$ in $A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])$ then we have $\Ad(a_{1}^{\circ})=\Ad(a_{2}^{\circ})$ , so $a_{1}^{\circ}=s\cdot a_{2}^{\circ}$ for some central unit $s\in(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])^{\times}$ . Now, again by Beauville-Laszlo, one has a natural embedding of the double quotient2323 23 Which corresponds to the gluing data for a line bundle on $\Spec R$ given by trivial line bundles on $\Spec R^{\wedge}_{h}$ and $\Spec R[h^{-1}]$ and the the gluing $R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]\simeq R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]$ for the restrictions to $\Spec R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]$ given by $s\in R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}]$ . $(R^{\wedge}_{h})^{\times}\backslash(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])^{\times}/R[h^{-1}]^{\times}$ to $\Pic(R)$ . Since $\Pic(R)=0$ by our assumption, it means that we can decompose $s\in(R^{\wedge}_{h}[h^{-1}])^{\times}$ as $s_{1}^{-1}s_{2}$ with $s_{1}\in(R^{\wedge}_{h})^{\times}$ and $s_{2}\in(R[h^{-1}])^{\times}$ . Replacing $a_{1}$ and $a_{2}$ by $s_{1}a_{1}$ and $s_{2}a_{2}$ we now get $a_{1}^{\circ}=a_{2}^{\circ}$ , while still $\phi_{1}=\Ad(a_{1})$ and $\phi_{1}=\Ad(a_{2})$ . Using Beauville-Laszlo one more time the data of $a_{1}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h})$ , $a_{2}\in A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}])$ with $a_{1}^{\circ}=a_{2}^{\circ}$ gives an element $a\in^{\times}$ . Moreover, the data of $\Ad(a_{1})\in\Aut_{R^{\wedge}_{h}}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R^{\wedge}_{h}))$ , $\Ad(a_{2})\in\Aut_{R[h^{-1}]}(A_{\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}}(R[h^{-1}]))$ is the same as for the $\phi$ . Thus, $\phi=\Ad(a)$ and we are done.

#### Remark 3.45.

From Proposition 3.44 we get an exact sequence of sheaves on $\Sch^{h-\mathrm{sep}{}}_{\!/\mathbb{S}}$ :

$$ 1\rightarrow{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\rightarrow\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}^{\times}\rightarrow\underline{\Aut}(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}})\xrightarrow{\mathsf{r}}G_{0}. $$

In fact if we restrict to even smaller subcategory of locally constant schemes (see some later section) one can show that the morphism $\mathsf{r}$ becomes surjective, and so we will have a 4-term exact sequence.

Further we will need the following corollary:

#### Corollary 3.46.

Let $T$ be an $\mathbb{F}_{p}$ -scheme and let $\pi\colon T\times\mathbb{S}\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ be the projection. Let $R$ be the stalk of ${\mathcal{O}}_{T\times\mathbb{S}}$ at a point $x\in T\times\mathbb{S}$ and consider the corresponding map $\Spec R\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ . Then every $R$ -linear automorphism of $\mathcal{A}_{\mathbb{S}}(R)$ that lies in $\Ker(\mathsf{r})(R)$ is inner.

#### Proof.

Note that $\Spec R\rightarrow\mathbb{S}$ is $h$ -separable. Indeed, either $\pi(x)=\{\infty\}$ and then $\Spec R$ lies over $\mathbb{S}\backslash\{0\}$ or $\pi(x)\in\mathbb{S}\backslash\{\infty\}$ and then $R$ is a localization of a $k[h]$ -algebra of the form Example 3.32(1) (and thus is also $h$ -separable). ∎

## 4. Quasi-coherent sheaves of abelian categories

### 4.1. Sheaves of categories.

For the duration of this section a category over a commutative ring $R$ means a cocomplete abelian category ${\mathcal{C}}$ together with a ring homomorphism $R\to\Center({\mathcal{C}})$ , where $\Center({\mathcal{C}})$ is the center of ${\mathcal{C}}$ , that is the ring of endomorphisms of the identity functor $\Id\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{C}}$ . Given such ${\mathcal{C}}$ and a homomorphism $R\to R^{\prime}$ define ${\mathcal{C}}\otimes_{R}R^{\prime}$ to be the category over $R^{\prime}$ formed by pairs $(M,\alpha)$ , where $M$ is an object of ${\mathcal{C}}$ and $\alpha\colon R^{\prime}\to\End(M)$ is a homomorphism of algebras over $R$ .

Recall the notion of a quasi-coherent sheaf of (abelian) categories over an algebraic stack due Gaitsgory ([G1, §9], [G2, §1]). Let $X$ be an algebraic stack (with respect to fpqc topology) over a base scheme $S$ such that the diagonal morphism $X\to X\times_{S}X$ is affine A quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ consists of the following data.

- (i) For every affine scheme $Z$ over $X$ a category ${\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ over ${\mathcal{O}}(Z)$ .

- (ii) For every morphism $u\colon Z^{\prime}\to Z$ of affine schemes over $X$ , an equivalence

$$ u^{*}\colon{\mathfrak{S}}(Z)\otimes_{{\mathcal{O}}(Z)}{\mathcal{O}}(Z^{\prime})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathfrak{S}}(Z^{\prime}), $$

of categories over ${\mathcal{O}}(Z^{\prime})$ .

- (iii) For every composable pair of morphisms $u_{1}$ , $u_{2}$ of affine schemes over $X$ , an isomorphism $(u_{1}\circ u_{2})^{*}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}u_{2}^{*}\circ u_{1}^{*}$ such that the natural compatibility axiom for $3$ -fold compositions holds.

Given a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ the category ${\mathfrak{S}}(X)$ of its global sections is defined to be $\mathop{\displaystyle\lim_{\longleftarrow}}{\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ , where the limit is taken over the category of affine schemes over $X$ . Given any morphism $u\colon Z\to X$ we shall write ${\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ for the category of global sections of the pullback of ${\mathfrak{S}}$ to $Z$ . According to [G2, Proposition 8] ${\mathfrak{S}}$ has the sheaf property: for a faithfully flat cover $u\colon Z\to X$ the category ${\mathfrak{S}}(X)$ is equivalent to the category of descent data on ${\mathfrak{S}}(Z)$ . A key result proven in is the faithfully flat descent for quasi-coherent sheaves of categories: for $u$ as above, giving a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $X$ is equivalent to giving a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $Z$ together with descent data.

Note that if $X=\Spec{\mathcal{O}}(X)$ is an affine scheme then giving a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ is equivalent to giving a category ${\mathfrak{S}}(S)$ over ${\mathcal{O}}(S)$ .

#### Example 4.1.

Let $A$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ -algebras. For a morphism $u\colon Z\to X$ , define a category $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z)$ to be the category of quasi-coherent sheaves of $u^{*}A$ -modules on $Z$ . This construction determines a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $X$ denoted by $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . In particular, ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $X$ with ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\QCoh(Z)$ , for any stack $Z$ mapping to $X$ .

### 4.2. Groups acting on a category.

For an affine group scheme $H$ over $S$ acting on $X$ and a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}$ over $X$ an $H$ -equivariant structure on ${\mathfrak{S}}$ consists of a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathfrak{S}}_{X/H}$ over the quotient stack $X/H$ together with an equivalence of quasi-coherent sheaves of categories between the pullback of ${\mathfrak{S}}_{X/H}$ to $X$ and ${\mathfrak{S}}$ . In particular, if $H$ acts trivially on $X$ we shall refer to the above data as an action of $H$ on ${\mathfrak{S}}$ .

The following construction will play an important role in what follows.

#### Construction 4.2 (A version of the Grothendieck construction).

$$ 1\to\underline{A}^{*}\to\widehat{H}_{X}\to H\times_{S}X\to 1 $$

be an extension of group schemes over $X$ together with an action

$$ \widehat{H}_{X}\to\underline{\Aut}(A) $$

of $\widehat{H}_{X}$ on $A$ by algebra automorphisms such that

- (T) the action of $\widehat{H}_{X}$ on $\underline{A}^{*}$ induced by (4.2) is equal to the adjoint action arising from exact sequence (4.1).

It follows that the restriction of homomorphism (4.2) to the subgroup $\underline{A}^{*}\subset\widehat{H}_{X}$ is equal to $\Ad$ . Indeed, (4.2) defines an action $\widehat{H}_{X}$ on $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ and we claim that the latter factors canonically through $H$ . Indeed, for an affine scheme over $X$ , $u\colon Z\to X$ , and an element $a\in\underline{A}^{*}(Z)\subset\widehat{H}(Z)$ the corresponding endofunctor $\phi_{a}$ of $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z)$ is induced by the inner automorphism $\Ad_{a}$ of $u^{*}A(Z)$ . Then $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}_{X/H}(Z)$ is the category of $\widehat{H}_{X}$ -equivariant quasi-coherent $A_{\mathcal{M}}$ -modules2525 25 A sheaf of $A_{\mathcal{M}}$ -modules is called quasi-coherent if the underlying sheaf of ${\mathcal{O}}_{{\mathcal{M}}}$ -modules is quasi-coherent. ${\mathcal{F}}$ on ${\mathcal{M}}$ such that the action of $\underline{A}^{*}$ on ${\mathcal{F}}$ induced by the $A_{\mathcal{M}}$ -module structure coincides with the action of the subgroup $\underline{A}^{*}\hookrightarrow\widehat{H}_{X}$ .

Assume that, for $f\colon Z\to X\times BH$ as above, we are given a $\widehat{H}_{X}$ -torsor $\widehat{\mathcal{M}}\to Z$ with $\widehat{\mathcal{M}}/\underline{A}^{*}={\mathcal{M}}$ . Using the action of $\widehat{H}_{X}$ on $A$ define a sheaf ${\mathcal{O}}_{Z}$ -algebras $O=\widehat{\mathcal{M}}\times^{\widehat{H}_{X}}A_{Z}$ . By definition, the category $O{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z)$ is equivalent to the category of $\widehat{H}_{X}$ -equivariant quasi-coherent modules over $A_{\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}$ . Repeating this construction for every scheme over $Z$ we get a functor between quasi-coherent sheaves of categories over $Z$ :

$$ f^{*}(A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}_{X/H})\to O{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}. $$

#### Proposition 4.3.

Morphism (4.3) is an equivalence. In particular, it induces an equivalence of categories $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}_{X/H}(Z)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}O{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z)$ .

#### Proof.

Thanks to the faithfully flat descent for quasi-coherent sheaves of categories it suffices to exhibit a fpqc cover of $Z^{\prime}\to Z$ such that functor (4.3) induces an equivalence of categories $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}_{X/H}(Z^{\prime})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}O{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}(Z^{\prime})$ . We take $u\colon Z^{\prime}=\widehat{\mathcal{M}}\to Z$ . Then both categories are identified with the category of quasi-coherent $A_{\widehat{\mathcal{M}}}$ -modules and morphism (4.3) evaluated at $\widehat{\mathcal{M}}$ is isomorphic to the identity functor. ∎

For example, assume that the projection $\widehat{H}_{X}\to H\times_{S}X$ has a section $H\times_{S}X\to\widehat{H}_{X}$ . Then the action of $H$ on $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ lifts to an action of $H$ on $A$ . Moreover, the section defines a lift $\widehat{\mathcal{M}}\to Z$ of ${\mathcal{M}}\to Z$ such that the corresponding sheaf of algebras is given by the formula $O={\mathcal{M}}\times^{H}A$ .

#### Remark 4.4.

Let $\phi$ be an action of $H$ on the category $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . In particular, for every scheme $Z$ over $X$ and a point $h\in H(Z)$ one has an autoequivalence $\phi_{h}$ of the category of $A_{Z}$ -modules. Assume fpqc locally on $Z$ this autoequivalence preserves the isomorphism class of the free $A_{Z}$ -module $A_{Z}$ . Then $\phi$ arises from data (4.1) and (4.2) for an appropriate $\widehat{H}_{X}$ . Namely, one sets $\widehat{H}_{X}(Z)$ to be the group of pairs $(h,\alpha_{h})$ , where $h\in H(Z)$ and $\alpha_{h}\colon\phi_{h}(A_{Z})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}A_{Z}$ is an isomorphism of $A_{Z}$ -modules.

#### Convention 4.5 (Quasi-coherent sheaves of categories over formal stacks).

Let $\hat{T}$ be an $h$ -adic formal stack, that is a collection of algebraic stacks $T_{m}$ over $S_{m}=\Spec{\mathbb{Z}}[[h]]/h^{m+1}$ , $m\geq 0$ , together with $T_{m+1}\times_{S_{m+1}}S_{m}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}T_{m}$ . A quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $\hat{T}$ is a collection $\{{\mathfrak{S}}_{m},i^{*}_{m}{\mathfrak{S}}_{m+1}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathfrak{S}}_{m},m\geq 0\}$ , where ${\mathfrak{S}}_{m}$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories over $T_{m}$ and $i^{*}_{m}{\mathfrak{S}}_{m+1}$ is the pullback of ${\mathfrak{S}}_{m+1}$ to $T_{m}$ .

## 5. Action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ .

### 5.1. Main Theorem.

The action of $G_{0}$ on $A_{0}$ defines its action on $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . The goal of this subsection is to extend the latter to an action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ .

#### Theorem 1.

Let $H$ be an affine group scheme over ${\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ equipped with a homomorphism $\upsilon\colon H\to G_{0}$ . There exists a unique (up to a unique isomorphism) action of the group scheme $H$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ equipped with a trivialization at $h=\infty$ such that the induced action of $H$ on the center of $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ (identified with $A_{0}$ ) equals the composition $H\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\upsilon}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{0}\hookrightarrow\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ .

#### Remark 5.1.

Set $H_{\mathbb{S}}=H\times\mathbb{S}$ . We claim that giving an action of $H$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ amounts specifying an extension

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{S}}}),} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Ad} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha} $$

satisfying property (T) in Construction 4.2. Indeed, using Remark 4.4 it suffices to check that, for any affine scheme $Z$ over $\mathbb{S}$ , every autoequivalence $\phi$ of the category ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z){\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ over ${\mathcal{O}}(Z)$ fpqc locally on $Z$ preserves the isomorphism class of the free ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ -module ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ . We shall see that this is true even Zariski locally on $Z$ . We may assume that ${\mathcal{O}}(Z)$ is a local ring. If the image of $Z$ in $\mathbb{S}$ does not contain $0$ then ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ is an Azumaya algebra. Hence, $\phi$ is given by the tensor product with a line bundle over $Z$ . Since $Z$ is local $\phi$ is isomorphic to the identity functor. If $Z\to\mathbb{S}$ maps the closed point to $0$ then ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ is a local ring. Hence, by Kaplansky’s theorem, every projective ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)$ -module is free. In particular, this can be applied to a projective module $\phi({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z))$ . Using that the ring of endomorphisms of $\phi({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z))$ is a local ring (namely, ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z)^{op}$ ) we conclude that $\phi({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}(Z))$ is indecomposable. This proves the claim. We remark that the argument above also shows that $\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}$ viewed as a $\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}$ -torsor over $H_{\mathbb{S}}$ is locally trivial for the Zariski topology on $H_{\mathbb{S}}$ .

Under this equivalence a trivialization of the action at $h=\infty$ amounts to the choice of a section $H=H\times\infty\to\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\infty$ whose image commutes with the subgroup $\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\infty\subset\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\infty$ . The action of $H=H\times 0$ on the center of $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is induced by $\alpha_{0}\colon\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}0\to\underline{\Aut}(A_{0})$ . The uniqueness part of Theorem 1 asserts that, for any two extensions (5.1), such that $\alpha_{0}$ equals the composition

$$ \widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}0\to H_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}0\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\upsilon}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{0}\subset\underline{\Aut}(A_{0}), $$

together with chosen sections at $h=\infty$ , there exists a unique isomorphism connecting the two that carries one section to the other.

#### Proof.

We start with the uniqueness assertion. Let $T$ be an affine scheme over ${\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ , $\pi\colon T\times{\mathbb{S}}\to\mathbb{S}$ the projection. The tensor product with a line bundle defines a functor

$$ \Pic(T\times\mathbb{S})\to\Aut(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}) $$

from the Picard groupoid of line bundles over $T\times\mathbb{S}$ to the groupoid of autoequivalences2626 26 The composition of autoequevalences makes $\Aut(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})$ into a group object in the category of groupoids. Functor (5.2) is a homomorphism of groups in groupoids. of the quasi-coherent sheaf of categories $\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ .

#### Lemma 5.2.

Functor (5.2) is fully faithful and its essential image consists of those autoequivalences ${\mathfrak{H}}\subset\Aut(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})$ that act identically on the center of $(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})_{|T\times 0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ (identified with $A_{0}\otimes{\mathcal{O}}(T)$ ).

#### Proof.

The only part that requires a proof is the essential surjectivity of the functor $\Pic(T\times\mathbb{S})\to{\mathfrak{H}}$ . Let $\phi$ be an autoequivalence in ${\mathfrak{H}}$ . We claim that $\phi$ , locally for the Zariski topology on $T\times\mathbb{S}$ , is isomorphic to $\Id$ . Indeed, as explained in Remark 5.1, every autoequivalence of $\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is, locally on $T\times\mathbb{S}$ , induced by an automorphism of $\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . Since $\phi\in{\mathfrak{H}}$ the latter automorphism is equal to $\Id$ modulo $h$ . Now the claim follows from Lemma 3.46. Assigning to every open subset $U\subset T\times\mathbb{S}$ the set of isomorphisms $\phi_{|U}\simeq\Id$ we define a torsor (for the Zariski topology) under the sheaf of central elements in $(\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})^{*}$ . The latter sheaf is equal to ${\mathcal{O}}^{*}_{\mathbb{S}\times T}$ . This defines a line bundle $L_{\phi}$ over $T\times\mathbb{S}$ such that $\phi$ is the tensor product with $L_{\phi}$ . ∎

Next, consider the groupoid ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ formed by pairs $(\phi,\alpha)$ , where $\phi\in{\mathfrak{H}}$ and $\alpha\colon\phi_{|T\times\infty}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Id$ . The equivalence $\Pic(T\times\mathbb{S})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathfrak{H}}$ induces an equivalence between ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ and the groupoid of line bundles over $T\times\mathbb{S}$ equipped with a trivialization at $T\times\infty$ . Since the Picard stack of $\mathbb{S}={\mathbb{P}}^{1}_{{\mathbb{F}}_{p}}$ is isomorphic to ${\mathbb{Z}}\times B{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ it follows that ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ is discrete and its $\pi_{0}$ is the group $H^{0}(T,{\mathbb{Z}})$ .

Returning to the proof of the uniqueness assertion recall that giving an action $\psi$ of $H$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is equivalent to giving descent data along the morphism $\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}\times BH$ . In particular, any action gives rise to an autoequivalence

$$ \phi\colon\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\pi^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}, $$

where $\pi\colon H\times\mathbb{S}\to\mathbb{S}$ is the projection. If $\phi_{1}$ , $\phi_{2}$ are equipped with trivializations at $h=\infty$ and induce the same action on the center of $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ then $\phi_{1}\circ\phi_{2}^{-1}$ is an object of ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ corresponding to some element $[\phi_{1}\circ\phi_{2}^{-1}]\in H^{0}(H,{\mathbb{Z}})$ . Using the cocycle isomorphisms related to $\phi_{i}$ it follows that $[\phi_{1}\circ\phi_{2}^{-1}]$ is, in fact, a group homomorphism $H\to{\mathbb{Z}}$ . The latter must be trivial because $H$ is assumed to be affine and, in particular, quasi-compact. We conclude that there is a unique isomorphism $\phi_{1}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\phi_{2}$ that commutes with trivializations at $H\times\infty$ . The discreteness of ${\mathfrak{H}}^{\prime}$ (applied to $T=H\times H$ ) implies that $\phi_{1}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\phi_{2}$ commutes with cocycle isomorphisms. This completes the proof of the uniqueness assertion of the Theorem.

$$ \alpha\colon\iota^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{op}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}} $$

such that, for every $i$ , $\alpha(x_{i})=x_{i}$ , $\alpha(y_{i})=y_{i}$ . Observe that, for any algebra ${\mathcal{C}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ , the group stack of autoequivalences of $\iota^{*}{\mathcal{C}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{op}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is that of ${\mathcal{C}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ pulled back by $\iota$ . It follows that there is an equivalence of categories between the groupoid of actions of $H$ on ${\mathcal{C}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ and on $\iota^{*}{\mathcal{C}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{op}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . Consequently, $\alpha$ defines an autoequivalence of the groupoid of actions of $H$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . We shall refer to the latter as twisting by $\alpha$ . Applying this autoequivalence to an action from Theorem 1 (equipped with a trivialization at $\infty$ ) we derive that its twist by $\alpha$ is uniquely isomorphic to the former one. We rephrase this using the language of group extensions from Remark 5.1: if the action is given by diagram 5.1 then there exists a unique isomorphism $\widehat{\tau}\colon\iota^{*}\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\to\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}$ fitting in the diagram

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\iota^{*}\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\iota^{*}\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces H_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\tau} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{\tau}} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Id} $$

in which the first row is the pullback of the second one via $\iota$ , $\tau(a)=\alpha(a)^{-1}$ , that commutes with the homomorphisms to $\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})=\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{op})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\alpha}}{{\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}}}\iota^{*}\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})$ and respects the sections at $\infty$ . In particular, restricting $\widehat{\tau}$ to $h=0$ , we find an involution $\widehat{\tau}_{0}$ of $\widehat{H}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\{0\}$ that carries $a\in A_{0}^{*}$ to $a^{-1}$ and equals the identity on the quotient $H$ . Applying this to the universal case $H=G_{0}$ , $\upsilon=\Id$ , and using that $G_{0}$ is connected and does not admit nontrivial extensions by $\mu_{2}$ we conclude that there exists a unique $\widehat{\tau}_{0}$ -invariant section

$$ G_{0}\to\widehat{G}_{{\mathbb{S}}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}\{0\}. $$

(A posteriori the same conclusion holds for any connected $H$ .) Section (5.11) identifies the $G_{0}$ -action on $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ with one induced by the tautological action of $G_{0}$ on $A_{0}$ .

### 5.3. A ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}$ -equivariant structure on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ .

The next proposition shows that the action of $G_{0}$ on the quasi-coherent sheaf of categories ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ constructed in Theorem 1 extends to an equivariant structure with respect to a larger group acting on $S$ . Define an action $\lambda\colon A_{0}\to A_{0}\otimes{\mathcal{O}}({\mathbb{G}}_{m})$ of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ on $A_{0}$ by the formulae

$$ \lambda(x_{i})=x_{i},\lambda(y_{i})=zy_{i},1\leq i\leq n. $$

Here $z$ denotes the coordinate on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . We have that $\lambda([\eta])=z[\eta]$ . Hence, the subgroup ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\subset\Aut(A_{0})$ normalizes $G_{0}$ . Denote by

$$ {\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}:={\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda}}G_{0}\subset\Aut(A_{0}) $$

the subgroup generated by $G_{0}$ and ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Endow $\mathbb{S}$ with an action $\chi$ of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ by homotheties: $\chi(h)=zh$ . The projection to the first factor defines an action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}$ on ${\mathbb{S}}$ . Formulae (5.12) yield a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant structure on sheaf of algebras ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . We denote by $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}$ the corresponding quasi-coherent sheaf of categories on the stack ${\mathbb{S}}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Since the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action on the fiber of ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ over the fixed point $\{\infty\}\in{\mathbb{S}}$ is trivial, we have that the restriction of $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}$ to $\{\infty\}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ is equivalent to ${\mathcal{O}}_{\{\infty\}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . Finally, let $q\colon{\mathbb{S}}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})$ by the morphism of stacks induced by the inclusion ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}$ .

#### Proposition 5.6.

There exists a unique (up to a unique equivalence) quasi-coherent sheaf of categories $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})}$ on the stack ${\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})$ equipped with equivalences

$$ \Theta\colon q^{*}(({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}, $$

$$ \Xi_{\infty}\colon(({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})})_{|\infty/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{\{\infty\}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}, $$

and an isomorphism $\varpi$ between the pullbacks of $\Xi_{\infty}$ and $\Theta$ to $\infty/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ , such that the action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}$ on the center of $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ induced by $\Theta$ comes from the embedding (5.13). Moreover, the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}$ -action on $A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is isomorphic to the one given by (5.13).

#### Remark 5.7.

Consider the diagram corresponding to the $G_{0}$ -action on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ (see Remark 5.1).

$$ {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces G_{0}\times{\mathbb{S}}} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces 1} {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}).} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces Ad} \scriptstyle{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\alpha} $$

Morphisms $\lambda$ , $\chi$ and $\Ad_{\lambda}$ determine a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant structure on all the group schemes displayed above except for $\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . The proposition asserts that there exists a unique ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant structure on $\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}$ that makes the whole diagram ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant and such that the section $G_{0}\times\infty\to\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{S}\infty$ commutes with the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action.

#### Proof.

We start with the existence assertion. Let $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}}$ be the quasi-coherent sheaf of categories on ${\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}$ constructed in Theorem 1. We construct the quadruple $(({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})},\Theta,\Xi_{\infty},\varpi)$ by specifying the descent data for $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}}$ along the morphism

$$ \pro\colon{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}\to{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0}). $$

Let $\pro_{{\mathbb{S}}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}},\chi\colon({\mathbb{S}}/G_{0})\times{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}$ be the projection and the action morphisms respectively. We have to construct an equivalence

$$ \pro_{{\mathbb{S}}/{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}^{*}(({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}})\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\chi^{*}(({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}}) $$

together with the cocycle datum. Note the ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant structure on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ identifies the pullback of the quasi-coherent sheaves in question to ${\mathbb{S}}\times{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ with ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ lifted along $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}\colon{\mathbb{S}}\times{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to{\mathbb{S}}$ . Thus, each quasi-coherent sheaf of categories determines an action of $G_{0}$ on $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ each of which comes with a trivialization over $\infty\times{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Using Remark 5.3 there exists a unique isomorphism between the two actions compatible with trivializations. This gives equivalence (5.15). Construction of the cocycle datum is left to the reader.

For uniqueness assertion, observe that if $(({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})},\Theta,\Xi_{\infty},\varpi)$ is a quadruple from the Proposition, then, by Theorem 1, $\pro^{*}(({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})})$ is equivalent to $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}}$ . Hence $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes G_{0})}$ arises from a descent data along $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}$ as above and our assertion also follows from “up to a unique isomorphism” part of Remark 5.3.

As in §5.2 to prove the last assertion of the Proposition it suffices to construct a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -invariant section $G_{0}\times 0\to\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}\times_{\mathbb{S}}0$ . In fact, the uniqueness of $\widehat{\tau}$ in (5.10) implies that the latter is ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant. It follows that the same is true for section (5.11). ∎

### 5.4. Further remarks.

The following corollary of Theorem 1 will be used in §6.4.

#### Proposition 5.8.

Let $f\colon T\to G_{0}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ be a morphism of schemes, $T_{0}\hookrightarrow T$ the scheme theoretic fiber of $f$ over $G_{0}\times 0$ . Then Zariski locally on $T$ there exists a morphism $g\colon T\to\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})$ such that $f_{|T_{0}}=g_{|T_{0}}$ .

#### Proof.

Consider the action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{S}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ from Theorem 1 and let

$$ 1\to\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}\to\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}\to G_{0}\times{\mathbb{S}}\to 1 $$

be the extension corresponding to this action by Remark 5.1. As explained in loc. cit. Zariski locally on $T$ the map $f$ admits a lifting $\tilde{f}\colon T\to\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . The composition of $\tilde{f}$ with $\alpha\colon\widehat{G}_{\mathbb{S}}\to\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}})$ does the job. ∎

#### Remark 5.9.

We claim that the action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ constructed above does not lift to an action on the algebra ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ even if ${\mathbb{S}}$ is replaced by the formal completion $\hat{\mathbb{S}}$ . To see this we shall prove that the surjection $r\colon G=\underline{\Aut}(A_{h})\twoheadrightarrow G_{0}$ has no sections i.e., group homomorphisms $s\colon G_{0}\to G$ with $r\circ s=\Id$ . Assuming the contrary consider the induced morphisms of the restricted Lie algebras. Write $k={\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ . The restricted Lie algebra $\Lie G_{0}$ is the algebra of Hamiltonian vector fields on $\Spec A_{0}$ ([BK, Lemma 3.3.]). It follows that $\Lie G$ , the restricted Lie algebra of $k[[h]]$ -linear derivations of the associative algebra $A_{h}$ , can be identified with the Lie subalgebra $\frac{1}{h}(A_{h}/k[[h]])\subset A_{h}(h^{-1})/k((h))$ :

$$ 0\to\tfrac{1}{h}k[[h]]\to\tfrac{1}{h}A_{h}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\ad}}{{\longrightarrow}}\operatorname{Der}A_{h}\to 0. $$

In particular, $\Lie G$ has the structure of restricted Lie algebra over $k[[h]]$ and the differential of $r$ is identified with projection

$$ dr\colon\Lie G\to\Lie G/h\Lie G=\Lie G_{0}. $$

Thus, $ds$ defines an isomorphism of restricted Lie algebras over $k[[h]]$

$$ \Lie G_{0}\otimes_{k}k[[h]]\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Lie G. $$

Consequently, we have $\Lie G_{0}\otimes_{k}k((h))\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Lie G\otimes_{k[[h]]}k((h))$ . The isomorphism $A_{h}(h^{-1})=\Mat_{p^{n}}(k((h)))$ identifies $\Lie G\otimes_{k[[h]]}k((h))$ with $\mathfrak{pgl}_{p^{n}}(\,k((h))\,)$ , the quotient of $\mathfrak{gl}_{p^{n}}(\,k((h))\,)$ by its center. It is shown in [BV, Lemma 4.4] that there exists a split surjection $G_{0}\to{\mathbb{G}}_{a}$ . This yields a nonzero homomorphism of restricted Lie algebras $\Lie G_{0}\otimes_{k}k((h))\to k((h))$ , where $k((h))$ is equipped with the zero $p$ -th power operation. We claim that $\mathfrak{pgl}_{p^{n}}(k((h)))$ does not admit such homomorphisms. Indeed, the quotient $\mathfrak{gl}/[\mathfrak{gl},\mathfrak{gl}]$ is the restricted Lie algebra of the multiplicative group. In particular, $p$ -th power operation on this quotient is non-trivial. This contradiction completes the proof.

## 6. Canonical quantization of $\QCoh(X)$ .

### 6.1. Construction of the canonical quantization and its uniqueness.

For the duration of this subsection let $S$ be a scheme over ${\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ with $p>2$ , and let $(X,[\eta])$ be a quasi-smooth scheme over $S$ equipped a restricted symplectic structure

$$ [\eta]\in H^{0}(X,\coker({\mathcal{O}}_{X}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle d}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Omega^{1}_{X/S})). $$

We shall also assume that the rank of the vector bundle $\Omega^{1}_{X/S}$ is constant, say, $2n$ , for some $n\in{\mathbb{Z}}$ . In particular, $d[\eta]=:\omega$ is a symplectic form on $X/S$ meaning that $\wedge^{n}\omega$ does not vanish. Let $\pi\colon{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\to X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ be the $G_{0}$ -torsor of Darboux frames (see Construction 2.68). Denote by $\xi\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\to BG_{0}$ the morphism corresponding to the latter. In Theorem 1 we constructed an action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ and the corresponding quasi-coherent sheaf of categories $({\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{{\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}}$ on ${\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}$ . Let $\QCoh_{h}$ be its pullback via the morphism $\xi\times\Id\colon X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}\to BG_{0}\times{\mathbb{S}}={\mathbb{S}}/G_{0}$ . The sheaf of categories $\QCoh_{h}$ is equipped with the following pieces of structure

- (i) An equivalences $\Theta\colon(\pi\times\Id)^{*}\QCoh_{h}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ of quasi-coherent sheaves of categories over ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ . Here $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}\colon{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}\to{\mathbb{S}}$ is the projection.

- (ii) An equivalences $\Xi_{\infty}\colon(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{\infty\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ of quasi-coherent sheaves of categories over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ together with an isomorphism $\varpi$ between the pullback of $\Xi_{\infty}$ to ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ and the restriction of $\Theta$ to ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\{\infty\}$ 2727 27 The restriction of $\Theta$ yields $\pi^{*}(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{\infty\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}(\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}})_{|{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\{\infty\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ , where the second equivalence comes from (3.17)..

and enjoys the following property

- (P) The isomorphism $\Center(\pi^{*}((\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}))\simeq\pro^{*}A_{0}$ descends to $\Center((\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}})\simeq F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ , where $F\colon X\to X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is the relative Frobenius morphism.

Part (i) comes from the construction of $\QCoh_{h}$ as a decent of $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ along ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}\to X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ . Part (ii) is induced by the trivialization of the $G_{0}$ -action on the fiber of ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ at $h=\infty$ . Lastly, property (P) is derived from the isomorphism $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}\simeq{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times^{G_{0}}A_{0}$ , where $A_{0}$ is equipped with the tautological action of $G_{0}$ . We shall refer to the quadruple $(\QCoh_{h},\Theta,\Xi_{\infty},\varpi)$ as the canonical quantization of $\QCoh(X)$ .

#### Proposition 6.1.

The quadruple $(\QCoh_{h},\Theta,\Xi_{\infty},\varpi)$ is uniquely characterized by property (P).

#### Proof.

Let $({\mathfrak{S}}_{i},\Theta_{i},\Xi_{\infty,i},\varpi_{i})$ , $i=1,2$ , be quadruples with property (P). We shall prove that there exists a unique equivalence (up to a unique isomorphism) connecting the two. The argument is similar to the proof of the uniqueness part of Theorem 1. Giving a pair $({\mathfrak{S}}_{i},\Theta_{i})$ is equivalent equivalent to specifying the descent data for $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ along the morphism ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}\to{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}/G_{0}\times{\mathbb{S}}=X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ . In particular, $({\mathfrak{S}}_{i},\Theta_{i})$ determines an autoequivalence $\phi_{i}$ of ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ lifted to $G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ . Property (P) implies that the composition $\phi_{1}\otimes\phi_{2}^{-1}$ acts as $\Id$ on the center of ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ pulled back to $G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\{0\}$ . Applying Lemma 5.2 we conclude that $\phi_{1}\otimes\phi_{2}^{-1}$ is the tensor product with a line bundle $L$ over $G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ . The equivalence $\Xi_{\infty,i}$ yields an isomorphism between $\phi_{i}$ restricted to $G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\{\infty\}$ and the identity functor. In turn, the latter determines a trivialization of $L$ restricted to $G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\infty$ . The groupoid of line bundles over $G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ equipped with a trivialization over $G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\{\infty\}$ is discrete and its $\pi_{0}$ is the group $H^{0}(G_{0}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]},{\mathbb{Z}})={\mathbb{Z}}$ . Finally, the cocycle constraint implies that $\phi_{i}$ and, hence, $\phi_{1}\otimes\phi_{2}^{-1}$ is isomorphic to $\Id$ when restricted to $1_{G_{0}}\times{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\{\infty\}$ . This defines a trivialization of $L$ . ∎

By property (P) $(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}$ has a $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ -linear structure. Moreover, by (i), locally for the fpqc topology, $(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}$ , as a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories with a $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ -linear structure, is equivalent to $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . We shall see that this also holds globally. To this end, observe that, for any ring $A$ , the groupoid of autoequivalences of $A{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ is identified with the groupoid of autoequivalences of $A^{op}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . In particular, the descent data for $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ along the morphism ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}\to X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ specified by $(\QCoh_{h},\Theta)$ determines a descent data for $\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{op}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . We denote $\QCoh_{h}^{\circ}$ the corresponding sheaf of categories over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ and by $\Theta^{\circ}\colon(\pi\times\Id)^{*}\QCoh_{h}^{\circ}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\pro_{\mathbb{S}}^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{op}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ the equivalence it comes with. Explicitly, $\QCoh_{h}^{\circ}$ assigns to each $Z\stackrel{{\scriptstyle u}}{{\longrightarrow}}X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ the category of all right exact ${\mathcal{O}}$ -linear functors $u^{*}\QCoh_{h}\to{\mathcal{O}}_{Z}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ that commute with all direct sums2828 28 To see this observe that, for any ring $A$ , the category of right $A$ -modules is equivalent to the category of right exact functors from left $A$ -modules to abelian groups that commute with all direct sums.. Equivalence $\Xi_{\infty}$ and isomorphism $\varpi$ determine $\Xi^{\circ}_{\infty}\colon(\QCoh_{h}^{\circ})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{\infty\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{O}}_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ , $\varpi^{\circ}$ . Next, recall from (5.9) an isomorphism $\alpha\colon\iota^{*}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}^{op}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}{\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ . By Proposition 6.1 there exists a unique equivalence of the triples

$$ \Sigma\colon(\QCoh_{h},\Theta,\Xi_{\infty},\varpi)\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}(({\Id}\times\iota)^{*}\QCoh_{h}^{\circ},\alpha\circ\Theta^{\circ},\Xi^{\circ}_{\infty},\varpi^{\circ}). $$

Denote by

$$ \Sigma_{0}\colon(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}(\QCoh_{h}^{\circ})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}} $$

the restriction of the latter to $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}$ . Observe that the pullback $\Sigma_{0}$ to ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times\{0\}$ is naturally isomorphic to the identity functor $\pro^{*}A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}\simeq\pro^{*}{A_{0}^{op}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . Every $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ -linear equivalence $\Xi_{0}\colon(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ induces $(\QCoh_{h}^{\circ})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ denoted by $\Xi_{0}^{\circ}$ .

#### Proposition 6.2.

There exists a unique triple $(\Xi_{0},\kappa,\upsilon)$ , where

$$ \Xi_{0}\colon(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}} $$

is a $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ -linear equivalence of quasi-coherent sheaves of categories over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ , $\kappa$ is an isomorphism between $\pi^{*}(\Xi_{0})$ and the composite

$$ \pi^{*}((\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Theta}}{{\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}}}\pro^{*}A_{0}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\pi^{*}(F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}){\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\pi^{*}(F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}), $$

and $\upsilon$ is an isomorphism $\Xi_{0}^{\circ}\circ\Sigma_{0}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}\Xi_{0}$ compatible with $\kappa$ .

#### Proof.

Locally, for the fpqc topology, $(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\}}$ , as a quasi-coherent sheaf of categories with a $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ -linear structure, is equivalent, to $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}$ . Assigning to a scheme over $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ the groupoid of such equivalences we define a gerbe on $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ banded by the group scheme of invertible elements in $F_{*}{\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ or, equivalently, a gerbe ${\mathcal{E}}$ on $X$ banded by ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . The equivalence $\Sigma_{0}$ amounts to specifying an isomorphism between ${\mathcal{E}}$ and the opposite gerbe i.e., the reduction of ${\mathcal{E}}$ to a gerbe ${\mathcal{E}}^{\prime}$ on $X$ banded by $\mu_{2}\subset{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . By construction the pullback of ${\mathcal{E}}^{\prime}$ to ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times_{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}X$ is trivialized. ### 6.2. ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant quantizations.

Let $S$ be a scheme over ${\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ with $p>2$ , and let $(X,\omega)$ be a scheme quasi-smooth over $S$ equipped with a symplectic $2$ -form $\omega\in\Omega^{2}_{X/S}(X)$ and a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action

$$ \gamma\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X\to X. $$

We assume that $\gamma$ is a morphism of schemes over $S$ and the following identity holds

$$ \gamma^{*}\omega=z^{m}\proj_{X}^{*}\omega, $$

for some integer $m$ invertible in ${\mathbb{F}}_{p}$ . Here $z$ denotes the coordinate on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ and $\proj_{X}\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X\to X$ the projection. The ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action on $X$ defines a homomorphism from the Lie algebra of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ to the Lie algebra of vector fields on $X$ . Denote by $\theta$ the image of the generator $z\frac{\partial}{\partial z}$ of $\Lie{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ . Formula (6.3) together with the identity $d\omega=0$ imply that

$$ d\iota_{\theta}\omega=m\omega. $$

Hence, $1$ -form $\eta=\frac{1}{m}\iota_{\theta}\omega$ , defines a restricted Poisson structure on $X$ . Observe that the composition

$$ {\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times{X^{(1)}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle F_{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}\times\Id}}{{\longrightarrow}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times{X^{(1)}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\gamma^{\prime}}}{{\longrightarrow}}{X^{(1)}}, $$

where $F_{{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}$ is the Frobenius morphism on ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ , carries the closed subscheme ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times{X^{(1)}}$ to $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\hookrightarrow{X^{(1)}}$ yielding a morphism

$$ \gamma_{p}\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\to X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}. $$

Endow $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ with a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -action given by $\gamma_{p}$ . Note that the Frobenius morphism $F\colon X\to X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}$ is ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant. Also, consider the action $\chi_{m}\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times{\mathbb{S}}\to{\mathbb{S}}$ given by the formula $\chi_{m}^{*}(h)=z^{m}h$ . We shall see that the canonical quantization $\QCoh_{h}$ comes equipped with a ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ -equivariant structure with respect to the diagonal action $(\gamma_{p},\chi_{m})\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\times(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}})\to X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ . Let us explain a construction of the corresponding quasi-coherent sheaf of categories $(\QCoh_{h})_{(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}})/_{\!\gamma_{p},\chi_{m}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}$ on the quotient stack $(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}})/_{\!\gamma_{p},\chi_{m}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

Recall from §5.3 the homomorphism $\lambda\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to\Aut(A_{0})$ and denote by $\lambda_{m}$ its pre-composition with the isogeny $t_{m}\colon{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ , $t^{*}_{m}(z)=z^{m}$ . The action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ on $A_{0}$ normalizes $G_{0}\subset\Aut(A_{0})$ . Denote by ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda_{m}}}G_{0}$ the corresponding semidirect product. Let $\pi\colon{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\to{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ be the $G_{0}$ -torsor of Darboux frames. Then, using $\lambda_{m}$ and $\gamma$ , the action of $G_{0}$ on ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ extends to an action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda_{m}}}G_{0}$ making $\pi$ equivariant with respect to this larger group. The product ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ equipped with diagonal action of ${\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda_{m}}}G_{0}$ yields a morphism of stacks

$$ (X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}})/_{\!\gamma_{p},\chi_{m}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\longrightarrow}\limits^{\sim}}({\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}})/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda_{m}}}G_{0})\to{\mathbb{S}}/_{\!\chi_{m}}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda_{m}}}G_{0}) $$

The homomorphism

$$ {\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda_{m}}}G_{0}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle t_{m}\times\Id}}{{\longrightarrow}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda}}G_{0} $$

and the identity map on ${\mathbb{S}}$ induce a morphism

$$ S/_{\!\chi_{m}}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda_{m}}}G_{0})\to{\mathbb{S}}/_{\!\chi}({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda}}G_{0}), $$

where $\chi=\chi_{0}$ . Let

$$ \overline{\xi}_{S}\colon(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}})/_{\!\gamma_{p},\chi_{m}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to{\mathbb{S}}/({\mathbb{G}}_{m}\ltimes_{\Ad_{\lambda}}G_{0}) $$

be the pre-composition of the latter with (6.5). By construction, the pullback of $(\QCoh_{h})_{(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}})/_{\!\gamma_{p},\chi_{m}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}$ to $X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}}$ is $\QCoh_{h}$ . Also, the category of global sections of $(\QCoh_{h})_{(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times{\mathbb{S}})/_{\!\gamma_{p},\chi_{m}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}}$ on $(X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\{0\})/_{\!\gamma_{p}}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ is the category of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X/_{\!\gamma}{\mathbb{G}}_{m}$ .

### 6.3. Quantizations of $\QCoh(X)$ vs quantizations of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$

In this subsection we shall explain how, under a certain assumption, (6.8) below, $(\QCoh_{h})_{|X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}\times\hat{\mathbb{S}}}$ can be described as modules over a Frobenius-constant quantization of the algebra ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ . For the sake of simplicity we shall assume that $S$ is the spectrum of a field $k$ of characteristic $p>2$ and $X$ is a smooth $S$ -scheme.

For an integer $l\geq 0$ , set $G_{l}=\coker((\underline{A}_{h}^{*})^{\geq l-1}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\Ad}}{{\longrightarrow}}G)$ , where $(\underline{A}_{h}^{*})^{\geq l-1}\subset\underline{A}_{h}^{*}$ is the subgroup of elements equal to $1$ modulo $h^{l}$ . Recall from [BK] that a Frobenius-constant quantization of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}$ of level $l$ is a $G_{l}$ -torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta],l}$ over ${X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ together with a $G_{l}$ -equivariant morphism ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta],l}\to{\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}$ of schemes over ${X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}$ . The latter determines a coherent sheaf of algebras $O_{l}={\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta],l}\times^{G_{l}}A_{h}/(h^{l+1})$ flat over ${\mathcal{O}}_{{X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}}[h]/(h^{l+1})$ . (Note that the canonical map $G_{l}\to\underline{\Aut}(A_{h}/(h^{l+1}))$ is not surjective. Consequently, the torsor ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta],l}$ carries more information than sheaf of algebras $O_{l}$ .) A section

$$ G_{0}\to G_{1} $$

of the projection $G_{1}\twoheadrightarrow G_{0}$ constructed in [BK] identifies the groupoid of level $1$ Frobenius-constant quantization with the groupoid of ${\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{*p}$ -torsors on the étale site of $X$ . Thus, every Frobenius-constant quantization $O_{l}$ , ( $l>0$ ), determines a class $\rho([O_{l}])\in H^{1}_{et}({X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}},{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{*}/{\mathcal{O}}_{X}^{*p})$ .

For every integer $l\geq 0$ , the following data are equivalent.

- (iii) An object $\underline{O}_{l}\in\QCoh_{h}({X^{\{\!\!\!\ p\ \!\!\!\}}}\times{\mathbb{S}}_{l})$ such that $\Theta(\pi\times\Id)^{*}(\underline{O}_{l})\in{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{S}}}{\operatorname{\mathsf{-Mod}}}({\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times{\mathbb{S}}_{l})$ is locally isomorphic to the free ${\mathcal{A}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ -module $\underline{{\mathcal{A}}}_{\mathbb{S}}$ pulled back to ${\mathcal{M}}_{X,[\eta]}\times S_{l}$ .

$(i)\Rightarrow(ii)$ . The morphism $\widehat{G}_{{\mathbb{S}}_{l}}\to\underline{\Aut}({\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{S}}_{l}})$ displayed in diagram (5.6) yields a coherent sheaf of algebras $O_{l}=\widehat{{\mathcal{M}}}_{X,[\eta],l}\times^{\widehat{G}_{{\mathbb{S}}_{l}}}{\mathcal{A}}_{{\mathbb{S}}_{l}}$ and Proposition 4.3 yields equivalence (6.7). $$ 1\to{\mathbb{G}}_{m}\to\widehat{G}_{{\mathbb{S}}_{0}}\to G_{1}\to 1. $$

#### Lemma 6.8.

The group $G_{0,J}$ is connected.

#### Proof.

The lemma follows. ∎
